questions.question: How many identical layers are stacked in the Transformer encoder?
questions.answer:
[3] (source: attention, page 3)
The Transformer follows this overall architecture using stacked self-attention and point-wise, fully connected layers for both the encoder and decoder, shown in the left and right halves of Figure 1, respectively.

questions.question: Why does scaled dot-product attention divide the dot products by the square root of d_k?
questions.answer:
[1], [2]

The dot products get large, and to counteract this effect, we scale the dot products by 1√dk. This is done to prevent the softmax function from having extremely small gradients.

questions.question: What are the two RAG model formulations introduced in the paper, and how do they differ?
questions.answer:
[2] and [5]. 

The two RAG model formulations introduced in the paper are RAG-Token and RAG-Sequence. They differ in their decoding procedure. RAG-Token uses a standard beam decoder with transition probability p′θ(yi|x,y1:i−1) = ∑z∈top-k(p(·|x))pη(zi|x)pθ(yi|x,zi,y1:i−1), whereas RAG-Sequence requires "Thorough Decoding" involving additional forward passes for each document z for which the generated hypothesis y does not appear in the beam.
questions.judge_reason: Missing key facts about how they differ.
